_comment: Places worth visiting, for the Discover view (discover.js): each with its own page (source_url, checked by hand on checked_on), a line in our words, and where it is with its nearest stops, filled from OpenStreetMap by scripts/locate_destinations.py. Curated, not every tourism tag in OpenStreetMap. Added 6 November 2026 at the maintainer's request. Location and wheelchair facts from OpenStreetMap are ODbL.

places.name: Brighton Palace Pier
places.line: The pier: rides, arcades and the view back along the seafront.
places.about: Brighton's pier, with a funfair of rides including a helter skelter, arcades, a restaurant, a bar and kiosks over the sea. Walking on is usually free, but the pier charges for entry at its busiest times.

photo.author: Arild Vågen
photo.alt: Brighton Palace Pier from the beach, stretching out to sea

places.name: Brighton i360
places.line: A glass viewing pod that rises high over the seafront by the West Pier.
places.about: A glass pod that climbs a slender tower on the seafront to 138 metres (450 feet), for a view along the coast and over the city. Tickets are needed; people living in some local postcodes can buy walk-up resident tickets.

photo.author: Arild Vågen
photo.alt: The i360 tower and its glass pod above the rusted columns of the old West Pier

places.name: Royal Pavilion & Garden
places.line: The Prince Regent's seaside palace, and its garden.
places.about: The Regency palace built for the Prince Regent, later George IV: Indian on the outside, its rooms in a Chinese style, set in its own garden in the middle of the city. Tickets are needed for the palace, with guided tours as well.

photo.author: Qmin
photo.alt: The Royal Pavilion's onion domes and minarets under a blue sky

places.name: Brighton Museum & Art Gallery
places.line: Art, design and the city's story, in the Royal Pavilion's garden.
places.about: Archaeology, fashion, photography and art, from the deep past to today, in the Royal Pavilion's garden, a short walk from the seafront. Its exhibitions change through the year.

photo.file: Brighton Museum and Art Gallery (IoE Code 480508).jpg
photo.author: The Voice of Hassocks
photo.alt: The museum's ornate entrance in the Royal Pavilion's garden

places.name: Preston Manor & Gardens
places.line: An Edwardian manor house and walled garden beside Preston Park.
places.about: An Edwardian house shown as the Stanford family's home, upstairs and downstairs, with its gardens beside Preston Park. Open in season (14 March to 30 November in 2026); payment by card only.

photo.file: Preston Manor, Preston Village, Brighton (from rear).JPG
photo.author: The Voice of Hassocks
photo.alt: Preston Manor, a long pale house, above a flint wall and lawn

places.name: Hove Museum of Creativity
places.line: Toys, film and craft, on New Church Road.
places.about: Hove's museum of creativity, in a Victorian villa on New Church Road: toys, film and crafts, with exhibitions that change through the year.

photo.file: Hove Museum and Art Gallery (Brooker Hall), New Church Road, Hove.jpg
photo.author: The Voice of Hassocks
photo.alt: Hove Museum, a yellow brick Victorian villa

places.name: Brighton Marina
places.line: Shops, restaurants and the harbour at the east end of the seafront.
places.about: Britain's largest marina, at the east end of the seafront: restaurants, shops, hotels and entertainment around its boardwalks and harbour.

photo.author: Jim Linwood
photo.alt: Brighton Marina's harbour and waterside houses from above

places.name: SEA LIFE Brighton
places.line: An aquarium in the Victorian arches beside the pier.
places.query: Sea Life Brighton, Marine Parade, Brighton
places.about: Opened in 1872 and designed by Eugenius Birch, it is the world's oldest aquarium still open: more than 5,000 creatures, sharks, turtles and jellyfish among them, under its restored Victorian arcade. Tickets are needed; booking online guarantees entry.

photo.file: The Brighton Aquarium And Attached Walls And Piers And Railings And Lamps.jpg
photo.author: Robert-brook
photo.alt: Steps down to the aquarium's entrance, lined with palms

places.name: Volk's Electric Railway
places.line: The Victorian electric railway along the beach towards Black Rock.
places.about: The world's oldest electric railway still running, for over 140 years, along the beach east of the pier. It closes for the winter; check its page for this season's dates.
places.photo_file: Train on the Volks Electric Railway, Brighton, Sussex - geograph.org.uk - 1811504.jpg

photo.file: Train on the Volks Electric Railway, Brighton, Sussex - geograph.org.uk - 1811504.jpg
photo.author: Peter Trimming
photo.alt: A Volk's Electric Railway car full of passengers beside the beach

places.name: Shoreham Fort
places.line: A Victorian fort at the mouth of the River Adur.
places.about: A Victorian fort guarding the mouth of the River Adur, restored from 1977 and looked after by the Friends of Shoreham Fort, a charity. It opens on set days: check its page before you go.

photo.author: Paul Gillett
photo.alt: The fort's red brick walls inside its grassy banks

places.name: Ropetackle Arts Centre
places.line: Music, comedy and film by the river in Shoreham.
places.about: A community-run arts centre and charity by the river in Shoreham: music, comedy, theatre and family shows, with the Rose Petal Café in its foyer.
places.photo_file: Ropetackle Arts Centre, Shoreham-by-Sea, West Sussex, July 2025 (1).jpg

photo.file: Ropetackle Arts Centre, Shoreham-by-Sea, West Sussex, July 2025 (1).jpg
photo.author: Gazamp
photo.alt: The Ropetackle building, with its tall sign, by a roundabout in Shoreham

places.name: Brighton City Airport
places.line: A working 1930s Art Deco airport terminal by the Adur.
places.about: Shoreham's airport, the oldest licensed aerodrome in the UK, first flown from in 1910. Its 1936 Art Deco terminal is still in use, and its restaurant, open every day, looks out over the planes.

photo.author: Peter Jeffery
photo.alt: The white Art Deco terminal across the airfield, light aircraft in front

places.name: Lancing College Chapel
places.line: A great Gothic chapel on the hill above the Adur.
places.about: A Gothic Revival chapel on the hill above the Adur, one of the most remarkable in England, and a landmark from miles around. Open to visitors daily, 10am to 4pm (noon on Sundays and bank holidays), except a few holidays.

photo.author: John Salmon
photo.alt: Lancing College Chapel, tall and Gothic, on a green lawn

places.name: Worthing Museum & Art Gallery
places.line: Costume, toys and local history, on Chapel Road.
places.about: Worthing's museum and art gallery on Chapel Road: costume, toys, archaeology and the town's history, with paintings and changing exhibitions.

photo.file: Worthing Museum and Art Gallery on a wet February lunchtime - geograph.org.uk - 1717464.jpg
photo.author: Basher Eyre
photo.alt: Worthing Museum's red brick front on a wet day

places.name: Cissbury Ring
places.line: An Iron Age hill fort on the Downs above Findon Valley.
places.about: The largest Iron Age hill fort in Sussex, with the hollows of far older flint mines inside it, on the Downs above Findon Valley. Looked after by the National Trust; from the bus it is a walk uphill.

photo.author: Simon Burchell
photo.alt: The grassy ramparts of Cissbury Ring, steps climbing one side

places.name: Worthing Pier
places.line: The town's Art Deco pier, with a theatre at one end and a pavilion at the other.
places.about: Opened in 1862, Worthing's Art Deco pier is Grade II listed and was UK Pier of the Year in 2019. The Pavilion Theatre and a bar are at the land end, an arcade halfway, and the South Pavilion out at sea; fishing from it is free.

photo.author: P L Chadwick
photo.alt: Worthing Pier and its amusements pavilion over the sea

places.name: Highdown Gardens
places.line: A garden made in an old chalk pit on the hill above Goring.
places.about: Sir Frederick and Lady Sybil Stern turned a chalk pit into a garden that now holds a National Plant Collection. Entry is free, with donations welcome. From the bus it is about a 20 minute walk, uphill at the end.

photo.author: Acabashi
photo.alt: A hibiscus in flower at Highdown Gardens

places.name: Stanmer Park
places.line: Brighton's biggest park, with a village, a great house and a walled garden.
places.about: A landscape laid out in the 1700s and a way into the South Downs National Park: Stanmer House, the 18th century village, and the Walled Garden at One Garden Brighton, with cafes and a play area. Accessible toilets, and a Changing Places toilet at One Garden Brighton.

photo.author: Rwendland
photo.alt: Stanmer House, a stone Georgian house, across its lawn

places.name: Devil's Dyke
places.line: A deep valley in the Downs north of Brighton, with views John Constable loved.
places.about: A legendary beauty spot on the South Downs: a valley nearly a mile long, the ramparts of an Iron Age hill fort, and a view Constable called the grandest in the world. The 77 from Brighton runs up daily in summer, and at weekends and bank holidays the rest of the year. Paths can be muddy after rain.

photo.author: Val Vannet
photo.alt: The Dyke's steep green valley winding through the Downs
